title: Superannuation Laws Amendment (Strengthening Trustee Arrangements) Bill 2017
short_title: Superannuation Laws Amendment (Strengthening Trustee Arrangements) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require regulated superannuation trustee boards to have an independent chair and at least one-third independent directors, replacing statutory equal representation requirements.
A new independence test would examine ownership and business relationships, with the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority able to determine whether particular people qualify as independent.
Existing trustees meeting transition conditions would generally have three years to comply, while self-managed funds and funds under specified acting trustees would be excluded.
changes: Groups of individual trustees would also need at least one-third independent members.
The independent chair would count towards the board's minimum number of independent directors.
Newly licensed trustees would have to meet the requirements when licensed.
The Commonwealth Superannuation Corporation's governance law would be amended to enable compliance with the independence requirements.
summary.affected: Regulated superannuation trustees, their directors, members and the Commonwealth Superannuation Corporation would be affected.
